ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced customer due diligence for politically exposed persons as defined under the AML/CFT Act 2009, screening against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the New Zealand Designated Persons List issued under the Sanctions Act 2019, New Zealand Police terrorist designations under the Terrorism Suppression Act 2002, and the United States OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List as a cross-border pre-incorporation benchmark.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office / New Zealand Companies Register (NZBN platform) — https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Companies Register operates in English. Company names must be in plain Latin or transliterated script, contain text that is not offensive or misleading, and must end with the word 'Limited' or the approved abbreviation 'Ltd'. Names using non-English script must be submitted in romanised form, and the Registrar may require a certified English translation where the meaning is not readily apparent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An approved company name reservation is valid for 20 working days from the date of approval. One extension of a further 20 working days may be filed online through the Companies Office before expiry. If the Registrar refuses a proposed name, the applicant may submit a name reconsideration request within 20 working days of the refusal decision, stating lawful grounds and attaching evidence that the name is not identical or confusingly similar and does not contain a prohibited or sensitive token. A refusal of reconsideration may be challenged by way of judicial review before the High Court of New Zealand.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Allowed conditionally: the registered office must be a physical street address in New Zealand, staffed and accessible during ordinary business hours, and capable of accepting service of legal and official documents; a bare post office box, mail-forwarding address, or unstaffed virtual address does not satisfy the Companies Act 1993. For a patent prosecution agency, a virtual office is acceptable only if the approved address is a genuinely operating New Zealand office and is used strictly as the statutory contact point; principal PCT and trademark prosecution files should be maintained at the physical professional premises of the New Zealand licensed patent attorney.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified baseline risk is low: approximately 3-5% per annum for a standard professional services company with a registered agent. The probability increases to about 20% if the company receives an AML/CFT suspicious activity report, has unexplained tax or financial anomalies, or presents shell-company indicators; unannounced inspections may be conducted by the Companies Office, the Financial Markets Authority, the Department of Internal Affairs, or the designated AML/CFT supervisor.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No. 105), ss. 12–19 (incorporation procedure and certificate), s. 22 (name restrictions), s. 26 (constitution), ss. 37–47 (classes of shares and issue), ss. 131–138 (directors' duties), s. 152 (requirements for directors), s. 153 (board decisions), s. 204 (registered office), ss. 378–382 (Registrar's powers); Income Tax Act 2007, subpart CW (foreign-sourced income exemption for non-resident-owned international business companies); Patents Act 2013 and Trade Marks Act 2002 (regulatory scope for IP prosecution).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, part of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), 15 Stout Street, Wellington 6011; online portal: New Zealand Companies Register (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form 1) under ss. 12 and 13 of the Companies Act 1993, integrated with the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) registration; including director and shareholder consents (Form 3 / Form 2 as applicable) submitted electronically via the Companies Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies under the Companies Act 1993; the Company may be incorporated with one or more shares of no par value. For the Tax-Exempt Zone classification of this International Company (CK_IC), the board shall maintain an issued and fully paid-up capital of NZD 1,000, represented by 1,000 ordinary shares held by a non-resident shareholder, thereby qualifying for the foreign-sourced income exemption under the Income Tax Act 2007. No escrow account, bank deposit certificate, or capital verification is required or accepted by the Registrar of Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (NZBN: [●]) — adopted by unanimous written consent on [date], pursuant to ss. 131, 153 and 190 of the Companies Act 1993. WHEREAS the Company was duly incorporated on [date], and the undersigned director(s) desire to organize the affairs of the Company; NOW THEREFORE IT IS RESOLVED THAT: (1) SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: the allotment and issue of 1,000 ordinary shares of no par value, subscribed at NZD 1.00 per share, be and is hereby approved, ratified and recorded in the Company's share register, creating a fully paid-up capital of NZD 1,000 held by the non-resident shareholder; (2) REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: the registered office of the Company be fixed at [street address, city, New Zealand], and the Registrar of Companies be directed to record the same as the registered office and service address under s. 204; the directors are authorized to appoint an agent at that address to accept service of documents; (3) OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: the following officers be and are hereby appointed: [name] as Managing Director, [name] as Company Secretary (optional), and [name] as Compliance Officer responsible for AML/CFT and patent attorney practice regulation under IPONZ; all officers shall act in accordance with the duties codified in ss. 131–138; (4) BANKING MANDATES: the directors be and are authorized to open corporate bank accounts, including the Official Patent Office Wire account and Wise Business account, and to execute all banking mandates, with the Managing Director and Company Secretary designated as joint signatories; (5) REGULATORY AUTHORIZATION: the directors be authorized to engage registered patent attorneys, execute client engagement agreements, file PCT applications with IPONZ and foreign offices, and take all steps necessary to carry on the business of an IP patent prosecution agency; (6) MEETING AND MINUTES: the board appoints a chairperson and adopts the default rules of procedure under s. 153, and records minutes of all proceedings. This resolution shall be filed with the Company records and is binding upon all shareholders and officers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability and Restricted Word Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — New Zealand Companies Register online search facility (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz / business.govt.nz).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a search of the Companies Register and NZBN database to confirm the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. Review the Registrar's guidelines under s. 22 of the Companies Act 1993; if the name contains restricted terms (e.g., 'bank', 'trust', 'assurance', 'national'), file a written application for prior approval from the Registrar with supporting evidence of consent or statutory authorization. The name should include the word 'Limited' (or its approved abbreviation). No notarization is required; the search and name clearance are fully electronic.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name in English and any related brand marks
Name availability search certificate or screen capture
Written justification for any restricted-word application
Consent letter from the objecting authority for restricted words (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or challenged, the incorporator may submit an alternative name through the same portal, file a formal 'Request for Reconsideration' to the Registrar within 20 working days under s. 366 of the Act, or apply for a name change under s. 24 after incorporation; the Registrar will issue a written decision and the party retains a right of appeal to the High Court of New Zealand under s. 370.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents and Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (electronic lodgement via the Companies Register); legal preparation by a licensed New Zealand law firm.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft or adopt the default constitution (Schedule 1 of the Companies Act 1993) or an opt-out custom constitution that replaces the default rules, in accordance with s. 26. Prepare and execute shareholder consent (Form 2) and director consent and certificate (Form 3), confirming eligibility under s. 152, including the requirement that at least one director be either ordinarily resident in New Zealand or a director of a registered company in a jurisdiction with which New Zealand maintains mutual recognition. Secure the physical registered-office address in New Zealand and the address for service. All consents must be signed by the appointees; electronic signatures are acceptable to the Companies Office.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (template not required at this step)
Company constitution (adopted form or bespoke)
Form 2 — Shareholder Consent and Agreement (signed)
Form 3 — Director Consent and Certification under s. 152 (signed)
Registered office physical address certificate or lease/letter from landlord or service provider
Board minutes approving the constitutional documents (pre-incorporation consent by subscriber)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries a director's residency or consent, the applicant shall provide supplementary evidence (e.g., statutory declaration, utility bill, passport) within 10 working days of the request; if the constitution is defective, file a correction or revoke and replace the constitution by special resolution under s. 29, and re-submit the incorporation application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office — Companies Register online filing system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online Incorporation Application (Form 1) on the Companies Register portal, populating the company name, registered office, address for service, director and shareholder details, share structure (1,000 ordinary shares at NZD 1.00), and the constitution election. Attach the signed Form 2, Form 3, and registered office consent. Pay the prescribed incorporation fee of NZD 150 (approximately USD 95) by credit card or bank debit. Submit the application electronically; the portal will validate against anti-money-laundering (AML) watchlists and the Registrar's screening rules. The application must be completed in English.
required_dossiers: Form 1 — Incorporation Application (completed online)
Form 2 — Shareholder Consent (attached)
Form 3 — Director Consent and Certificate (attached)
Company constitution (if adopting an opt-out constitution)
Registered office address and address for service details
Proof of payment of incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a Notice of Further Information under s. 18, respond in writing with the requested documents within 20 working days; failure to respond renders the application withdrawn. Upon withdrawing, the applicant may re-file a corrected Form 1 with a fresh fee. Any adverse name direction may be challenged by judicial review or statutory appeal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (via Companies Register and NZBN registry).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation under s. 19 of the Companies Act 1993, recording the company name, registration number, and date of incorporation, and the Companies Register automatically issues a 13-digit NZBN, which serves as the company's unique identifier across government agencies. Download and retain the electronic Certificate and the NZBN record; these instruments are conclusive evidence of incorporation. The company becomes a separate legal entity with perpetual succession on the date stated in the certificate. Any subsequent correction of certificate particulars (e.g., name spelling) must be applied for under s. 364.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (issued electronically)
NZBN Certificate of Registration (issued electronically)
Company's share register excerpt (kept internally)
Payment receipt for incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains an error or is defaced, apply to the Registrar for a corrected certificate under s. 364, providing a statutory declaration and the original certificate; the Registrar will revoke and reissue the certificate within 5 working days without additional fee, preserving the original incorporation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with the Inland Revenue Department (IRD Number, GST, and Employer Registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand — online via 'myIR' portal or electronic filing through accounting software.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NZBN, register the company for an IRD number for income tax with Inland Revenue (Form IR596 or online). Register for GST under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 if projected taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000 per year or voluntarily for input credit recovery. If the company will employ staff in New Zealand, register as an employer for PAYE, ACC and KiwiSaver deductions. Provide the Certificate of Incorporation, NZBN, director's IRD number and tax file number declaration, and the registered office address. Obtain a tax file number confirmation and the GST registration certificate, and maintain records of the tax-exempt-zone claim for the foreign-sourced income exemption (Income Tax Act 2007, s. CW 1).
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN Certificate
IRD registration application (IR596) or online 'Company and other entity registration' form
Director's identification and IRD/TFN declaration
GST registration application (if applicable)
Constitution and board resolution confirming tax classification
Foreign shareholder non-residency evidence (for tax-exempt-zone classification)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IRD queries the classification or the non-resident shareholder status, provide a written explanation supported by the board resolution and a notarized certificate of tax residency from the shareholder's jurisdiction within 20 working days; late registrations may be cured by filing combined disclosures with penalty remission under Part 9 of the Tax Administration Act 1994, and any adverse assessment can be objected to under s. 89K.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Corporate Bank Accounts and Payment Rail Activation (Official Patent Office Wire and Wise)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks (e.g., ANZ, ASB, BNZ, Westpac NZ) and licensed non-bank payment providers (Wise); AML/CFT compliance under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following incorporation, present the Certificate of Incorporation, NZBN, company constitution, and board resolution to the chosen bank or payment provider. Complete customer due diligence (CDD) with certified copies of director and shareholder passports, proof of residential address, source-of-funds declaration, and the corporate structure chart. Open a New Zealand dollar corporate account for ordinary operations and establish the 'Official Patent Office Wire' settlement account for outbound fees to IPONZ and foreign patent offices, and a Wise Business account for low-cost cross-border receipts and payments. Authorize joint signatory mandates (Managing Director and Company Secretary) and enable dual-approval for wire transfers above NZD 10,000.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN Certificate
Company constitution and first board resolution (banking mandate)
Certified passport copies of all directors and beneficial owners
Proof of residential address (utility bill dated within 3 months)
Source of funds and source of wealth declaration
Corporate chart and shareholder register extract
AML/CFT risk assessment form (bank-specific)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the account application is deferred or rejected, the applicant shall supplement CDD documentation, respond to the bank's enhanced due diligence questionnaire within 14 days, or apply to another licensed provider; unresolved SAR reporting decisions may be escalated to the Financial Intelligence Unit (NZ Police) only in lawful circumstances, and any unreasonable denial may be appealed through the Banking Ombudsman Scheme.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Annual Return Compliance, Registered Office Maintenance, and Ongoing Governance Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (for annual returns and director/address updates); Inland Revenue (for annual income tax filings).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and file the company's annual return (the 'Annual Return' under s. 242 of the Companies Act 1993) within the month nominated on the certificate, confirming the director, shareholder, registered office, and address for service; pay the annual return fee (approximately NZD 47.60). Update the Companies Register for any change of directors, registered office, or constitution via the appropriate online forms (e.g., Notice of Change of Registered Office; Change of Director Form). If the company is not eligible for an exemption under s. 3 of the Financial Reporting Act 2013, prepare financial statements that satisfy generally accepted accounting practice (NZ IFRS or reduced disclosure regime for small and medium entities). File the income tax return (IR4) annually with IRD and maintain the tax-exempt-zone status records.
required_dossiers: Annual Return form (online)
Financial statements (if required)
IR4 income tax return
Notice of Change of Registered Office or Director (if applicable)
Minutes of annual general meeting or board meeting
GST return (if registered, at applicable frequency)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an annual return is filed late, pay the late filing penalty (NZD 86.80) and file immediately; the Registrar may strike off the company under s. 318 for default, in which case the company may be restored under s. 329 by court order or curator application; the Registrar's refusal to accept a return may be corrected by re-presentation or by an application to the High Court for declaratory relief under s. 370.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Intellectual Property Office of New Zealand (IPONZ), a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), in partnership with the Patents Attorneys and Trade Marks Attorneys Registration Boards.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registration as a 'Licensed Patent Attorney Practice' under the Patents Act 2013 (ss. 154–160), with each natural-person patent attorney holding a current Certificate of Registration on the Register of Patent Attorneys maintained by the Patents Attorneys Registration Board (administered through IPONZ); the entity further obtains an 'IP Practice Accreditation' from IPONZ to transact electronically as an agent (via the IPONZ Case Management Portal) for filing, prosecuting, and managing PCT patent applications and international trademark registrations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand, operating under the Resource Management Act 1991 and the Waste Minimisation Act 2008; with regional district councils exercising delegated consent powers.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Tier 3 — Exempt / Registration-only for office-based professional services: the patent prosecution agency conducts no scheduled industrial activity, manufacturing, or discharge of contaminants requiring a full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) report. The operation is classified as a 'Permitted Activity' under the relevant District Plan; a low-impact 'Surface Water Discharge Registration' may be required from the regional council for the building's stormwater connection, and a formal EIA is not mandated under Schedule 4 of the RMA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No specific VOC, particulate, or wastewater discharge limits apply to administrative IP offices. General compliance is required with: national ambient air quality standards under the Resource Management (National Environmental Standards for Air Quality) Regulations 2004; wastewater discharge to sewer must comply with the local council's trade waste bylaw (pH 6–10, BOD < 600 mg/L, no heavy metals); confidential and e-waste (toner cartridges, electronic hardware) must be handled under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 with a licensed waste contractor; stormwater discharge must be free of visible contaminants, biodegradable residues, and hazardous substances under s. 15(1)(c) RMA.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification: the premises must obtain a Fire Evacuation Scheme approval from Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) and an annual fire safety compliance certificate under the Building Act 2004 (means of escape, fire alarms, extinguishers). Structural and Occupancy Clearance: a Code of Compliance Certificate (CCC) or existing Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) from the territorial authority, confirming structural load compliance, adequate seismic rating, and disability access under the Building Code. Occupational Health and Safety: workplace clearance and self-assessment under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 (HSWA) and WorkSafe New Zealand regulatory oversight, including a written health and safety policy, a risk register covering ergonomic and electrical hazards, first-aid provisions, and mandatory registration with the Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC) for the worker levy classification 'Office-Based Professional Services' (risk class low).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD / Te Tari Taake) — online portal myIR (https://myir.ird.govt.nz); New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) issued through the New Zealand Companies Office; export controls administered by the New Zealand Customs Service via the Trade Single Window
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident International Company: (1) apply for an NZBN through the NZ Companies Office; (2) if carrying on business in New Zealand, register as an overseas company under the Companies Act 1993 unless exempt; (3) apply for an IRD number using form IR 742 (Non-Resident Company IRD Number Application) or through myIR; (4) register for GST in myIR where the statutory NZD 60,000 taxable-supplies threshold is met; (5) use the single IRD number as the common taxpayer identifier for income tax, GST, RWT, and any employer obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — as a non-resident International Company (CK_IC), the entity is outside the New Zealand income tax net with respect to offshore patent-prosecution and international trademark-registration revenue, provided it maintains no fixed establishment or permanent establishment in New Zealand and derives no New Zealand-sourced income. Registration for New Zealand GST (where applicable) creates a GST identity only and does not alter the entity's non-resident income-tax status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box election. Available statutory elections and mechanisms include: voluntary GST registration under s 51 Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; GST grouping election under ss 55–57 GST Act 1985; election to account for GST on a payments (cash) basis or invoice basis under s 19 GST Act 1985; look-through company (LTC) election under subpart HB Income Tax Act 2007 (not applicable to a foreign International Company); CFC income attribution elections under ss EX 57–58 Income Tax Act 2007; and branch-equivalent or PE election mechanisms under applicable double-tax agreements. Hybrid mismatch rules under Part FH Income Tax Act 2007 are mandatory anti-avoidance provisions with no elective opt-out.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms_note: No check-the-box regime exists in New Zealand; entity classification follows the foreign legal form and NZ domestic characterization rules. The entity may elect into GST registration voluntarily, and may elect GST accounting basis, but cannot elect out of Part FH hybrid mismatch rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax) — a VAT-style consumption tax under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 (NZ)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in the preceding or current 12-month period (s 51 GST Act 1985); non-resident suppliers of remote services to New Zealand consumers are likewise required to register once their NZ taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000; voluntary registration is available below the threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping obligation. New Zealand has adopted the Peppol interoperability framework for e-invoicing, operational since 30 March 2022, on a voluntary basis; IRD accepts Peppol BIS 3.0 e-invoices. For goods exports, lodgement of export declarations through the Customs Trade Single Window is mandatory, but this is a customs process and does not constitute a GST clearance or digital stamping mechanism.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rated under s 11(1) GST Act 1985 where the supplier is GST-registered and the goods are exported within 28 days of the supply. Services: zero-rated under s 11A GST Act 1985 where the recipient is a non-resident who is not in New Zealand at the time of supply, the services are performed remotely or otherwise consumed offshore, and the supplier holds sufficient documentary evidence. Patent prosecution and international trademark registration services supplied to non-resident IP owners qualify for zero-rating where the intellectual-property rights are sought, protected, or exploited outside New Zealand or the services are enjoyed offshore.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged through the New Zealand Trade Single Window (applicable to physical goods exports)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing exportation within 28 days of the supply
Signed service agreement or engagement contract identifying the non-resident client and the applicable offshore IP jurisdiction
Tax invoice together with the supplier-held documentary evidence file required under s 11A(2)(c) GST Act 1985
Bank remittance advice or SWIFT MT103 evidencing payment from the non-resident client
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: IRD may retrospectively assess output GST at 15% plus use-of-money interest (UOMI) where zero-rating evidence is inadequate, the supply is recharacterised as domestic, or the export conditionality is breached. Shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 apply at graduated rates: unacceptable tax position 20%, gross carelessness 40%, and evasion or intentional misrepresentation 150%. Criminal prosecution for fraud or evasion may result in fines up to NZD 250,000 for a company and/or imprisonment of up to 5 years (ss 143A–143B TAA 1994). The standard four-year assessment time bar applies, but no time bar applies to assessments involving fraudulent or deceptive conduct.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua); external administration oversight by the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) and the Overseas Investment Office (OIO) for restricted inward direct investment
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a fully liberalised current and capital account. The NZD is freely convertible onshore and offshore. There are no exchange control approvals or profit repatriation permits. Dividends, royalties, patent prosecution fees, and IP licensing remittances may be transferred abroad without foreign exchange restriction. Non-resident shareholders and IP beneficiaries must comply with domestic withholding tax (non-resident withholding tax on dividends, royalties under Schedule 3 of the Income Tax Act 2007) and, where applicable, the Overseas Investment Act 2005 for investments in sensitive land or significant business assets. A nontransparent tax-exempt entity classification may trigger enhanced scrutiny under New Zealand anti-avoidance and anti-money-laundering rules, but does not impose currency convertibility blockers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds. New Zealand does not mandate conversion to NZD and does not impose a repatriation timeline. Exporters and service providers may hold foreign currency earnings onshore or offshore. However, AML/CFT transaction reporting obligations apply for cash transactions above NZD 10,000 and for cross-border wire transfers in accordance with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. Patent prosecution agencies receiving international reimbursements must maintain documentary evidence of the underlying official patent office invoices and client agreements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (ANZ) New Zealand
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Transaction Account plus Client Trust/Escrow Account for Official Patent Office Funding
Tier 1 Operational Account and Trust/Settlement Account
Premium Business Account with segregated Client Funds Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Conditional Feasibility. Authorised non-bank electronic money institutions and digital money remitters, notably Wise (formerly TransferWise) and Airwallex, hold Financial Service Provider (FSP) registration and are subject to the AML/CFT Act 2009. They can provide efficient low-latency cross-border payment rails for international patent office wires and client disbursements, particularly for low-risk recurring fee flows denominated in NZD, USD, GBP, EUR, and JPY. Legal constraints: they are not licensed as registered banks under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989; they cannot operate statutory client money trust accounts for a legal practice, and they may reject entities with beneficial ownership in high-risk jurisdictions or with tax-exempt offshore status. Therefore, a fintech EMI should be deployed as a secondary disbursement rail, never as the primary corporate treasury account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is generally permissible for a non-resident-owned New Zealand International Company, provided the entity has no New Zealand tax avoidance profile. The bank may require a video conference interview with at least two directors and the ultimate beneficial owner. Identity and address verification must be completed through a certified notary public or qualified legal professional, with original documents apostilled or chain-certified. The physical presence of directors in New Zealand is not an absolute statutory mandate, but a lower-tier branch or compliance-officer override may be imposed if the beneficial owner resides in or the entity is a resident of a Cook Islands-style international tax-exempt jurisdiction. The optimal strategy is to appoint a New Zealand-resident professional director and a registered office with substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of ultimate beneficial ownership through shareholder nominee arrangements, bearer instruments, or offshore trust structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered UBO register extract; certificate of incorporation and current company search; declaration of trust and nominee agreement; notarized passports of all natural persons above the 10% threshold; bank-source wealth and source-of-funds statement; independent legal opinion on ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt or zero-tax 'International Company' status flagged as prima facie tax avoidance or CRS/FATCA opaque interposition under New Zealand anti-avoidance jurisprudence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed tax counsel memorandum confirming the entity is not tax resident in New Zealand and is entitled to an exemption under the applicable international company regime; proof of economic substance in the home exempting jurisdiction (physical office, employees, client contracts); IRD Non-Resident Tax Registration Certificate; completed CRS self-certification forms and FATCA entity classification; contemporaneous board minutes showing commercial rationale for the entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire flows labelled with PCT, USPTO, WIPO, or official patent office references trigger sanctions screening and country-of-benefit mismatch alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copies of the IP prosecution agency retainer agreements; official patent office fee schedule and invoices; correspondences from national IP offices showing client case references; explanation of the flow of funds (inbound from client, outbound to Office); sanctions screening results from a trusted commercial compliance utility; declarations that no sanctioned party or country supports the underlying patent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Client funds held in escrow on behalf of foreign patent applicants may trigger the Financial Markets Conduct Act trust-money obligations if not routed through a registered bank trust account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed trust deed and escrow agreement; bank confirmation of a segregated client money account designation; professional indemnity insurance certificate; annual assurance audit of client trust accounts; regulatory notification or exemption letter, if applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection must be effected via SWIFT MT103 (or equivalent FAST/clearing message) from the non-resident shareholder's overseas bank to the New Zealand entity's NZD or foreign-currency operating account. The purpose code in the remittance instructions should be 'EC' (Equity Capital) or 'SI' (Shareholder Investment) on bank-specific inward remittance forms, accompanied by the board resolution authorising the issue of shares, updated company extract showing the shareholder, and, where required, OIO consent memoranda if the subscribed capital is applied to acquire sensitive commercial assets or land. If the entity is a tax-exempt international company with no New Zealand economic nexus, the injection should be labelled as a pure shareholder capital contribution and must be supported by source-of-funds evidence sufficient to prove no tax motivated avoidance or disguised Australian/Chinese taxable income.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade and official fee settlements should be executed using the following rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 directly from the NZ corporate account to WIPO/IPONZ/USPTO/EUIPO designated receiving accounts for official patent and trademark fees, referencing the IP case number and invoice line; (ii) SWIFT MT103 or domestic high-value clearing to the patent prosecution agent's own dedicated foreign currency account when paying in local currency; (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) are not advisable and are not structurally appropriate for professional services or intellectual property fees; the correct instrument is the professional invoice coupled with an irrevocable payment instruction. All outbound instructions must include the full SWIFT BIC of the counterparty, the invoice amount, the official fee suspense ledger reference, and the underlying PCT/patent/trademark application number. Same-day NZD settlement can be routed through the ESAS (Exchange Settlement Account System) and Cornercard? For cross-border, always use correspondent-cleared MT103 and retain SWIFT field 70 reference to the legal contract.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/GBP, and NZD/AUD forward contracts with onshore registered banks
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted or thinly traded emerging market currencies (e.g., NZD/CNH, NZD/INR, NZD/IDR) arranged via a licensed NZ bank or its offshore branch
FX swaps for temporary liquidity conversion without balance-sheet exposure
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for medium-tenor hedges of anticipated patent-fee escalation liabilities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Companies Act 1993, s.214) confirming company name, registered office, address for service, director particulars, and shareholding as at the annual return date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the date the Registrar issues the annual return form, normally aligned to the anniversary of incorporation; filing is completed online through the Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Reminder notices followed by the Registrar's strike-off procedure under s.316 of the Companies Act 1993, comprising Gazette notice, objection window, and removal from the register; a struck-off company loses limited liability protections and directors may incur personal liability for obligations arising after removal

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Significant Owner (UBO) Confirmation under the Companies (Disclosure of Beneficial Ownership) Amendment Act 2023, reconciling the internal register of significant owners with register-held data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Registrar of Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 working days of the anniversary of incorporation, with the first confirmation cycle applying once the beneficial ownership register obligations are in force from 1 May 2025
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence punishable by a fine of up to NZD 50,000 (approximately USD 31,000) for the company and NZD 10,000 per director; continuing default may additionally expose the entity to the Registrar's strike-off procedures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and, where the entity ceases to be exempt, the independent auditor's report prepared under NZ GAAP with reduced disclosure regime applied
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Registrar of Companies, via the Companies Register annual filing channel
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a non-issuer, the balance date is typically 31 March; the board must sign and date financial statements within six months of balance date and file them within 20 working days of signing; a small exempt company files only the Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors in default face fines of up to NZD 10,000 (approximately USD 6,200) plus continuing daily penalties of NZD 500 per day under the Companies Act 1993; the Registrar may also obtain court-ordered compliance and initiate removal-from-register action

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual tax compliance confirmation covering nil corporate income tax return status for the tax-exempt International Company and, where the entity is GST-registered for New Zealand taxable activities, periodical GST returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand (IRD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Income tax returns are required only upon IRD notice, generally due by 7 July following a 31 March balance date; GST returns are due by the 28th day of the month following each one-month or six-month taxable period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Tax Administration Act 1994, late income tax filing incurs penalties of NZD 250 rising to NZD 500 plus use-of-money interest; GST late filing penalties range from NZD 250 to NZD 1,000 plus interest; these sanctions do not apply where the entity validly establishes tax-exempt status with nil returns

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory audit and filed audited financial statements arise only where the company is not an exempt company, i.e. it has 10 or more shareholders at balance date, or it qualifies as 'large' under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 by exceeding at least one of: total assets NZD 60 million, total revenue NZD 30 million, or 50 full-time equivalent employees, in each of the two preceding accounting periods; a patent prosecution agency with fewer than 10 shareholders and below these thresholds is exempt from audit and filing
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand generally accepted accounting practice (NZ GAAP), comprising NZ IFRS for large for-profit entities and NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR) or the New Zealand Equivalent to the IFRS for SMEs framework for smaller entities, applied on a true and fair view basis under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and Companies Act 1993

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, within 15 working days of the incorporation anniversary, the company must confirm its significant owners (any natural person holding 25% or more of shares or voting rights, or exercising significant control) through the online Companies Register; the annual confirmation must reconcile with the internally maintained Significant Owner Register, and any share-transfer-driven change in beneficial ownership during the year must additionally be notified to the Registrar within 15 working days of the transaction and recorded internally before the confirmation is submitted
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (share ledger recording issued shares and all transfers)
Register of Directors (names, residential addresses, and consents to act)
Register of Significant Owners (UBO Register maintained in accordance with the 2023 Amendment Act)
Register of Charges (security interests over company assets, where any exist)
Minute Book (resolutions and minutes of board meetings, general meetings, and written shareholder resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350–1,200 per annum (NZD 550–2,000) for a licensed New Zealand registered office and corporate secretarial agent, inclusive of Annual Return preparation and UBO confirmation filing assistance; premium pricing applies where the agent maintains complex IP licensing registers or multi-jurisdictional ownership structures
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500–7,500 (NZD 4,000–12,000) for a certified independent audit of a typical SME patent prosecution agency under NZ IFRS RDR; additional scoping of USD 1,500–3,000 applies where the audit opinion must cover international patent portfolio schedules, PCT fee reconciliations, or consolidated group structures
